rawFindings.title: SHA is now computed from the unprocessed buffer instead of final preprocessor output
rawFindings.explanation: `file.sha` is assigned immediately after reading the source file, before any preprocessors run. For any file that is transformed (for example, CoffeeScript compiled to JS), the SHA no longer matches the content that Karma serves and uses to detect changes/caching.
rawFindings.suggestion: Move the SHA assignment back to the terminal preprocessor callback so it hashes the final `content` that will be served.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With a preprocessor that changes `/some/a.js` from `alert(1)` to `alert(1)-processed`, `file.sha` still hashes `alert(1)` instead of the served output, so consumers comparing SHA values see the wrong hash.
